ex: The dissident spent ten years in prison for his ideas.
Many dissidents had to leave the country to stay safe.
She was a famous dissident and also a writer.
The government watched the dissidents very closely.
The pancreas makes insulin to control your blood sugar.
The doctor checked her pancreas with an ultrasound.
The pancreas is a small organ behind the stomach.
He went to the hospital with a problem in his pancreas.
The mechanic cleaned the carburetor, and now the car starts.
Many old cars and motorcycles have a carburetor.
The carburetor on my lawn mower is dirty again.
A bad carburetor can make the engine stop.
Sexism at work is still a big problem.
She often speaks against sexism in sports.
Many people criticized the ad for its sexism.
Teachers should talk about sexism in schools.
sexism.note: Uncountable: a lot of sexism (not "a sexism").

compatriot.note: Formal; "fellow countryman" or "people from my country" is common.

ex: Some people avoid foods that contain GMOs.
Farmers here are not allowed to grow GMOs.
The label says the product has no GMOs.
Scientists still argue about the safety of GMOs.
Some big whales eat only tiny plankton.
Plankton lives in oceans, lakes, and rivers.
Many fish depend on plankton for food.
You need a microscope to see most plankton.
plankton.note: Uncountable: some plankton, a lot of plankton (not "a plankton").

ex: He has a second dan in karate now.
She got her first dan after five years of training.
To get a higher dan, you must train for years.
Our coach has a fifth dan in judo.
dan.note: Most often "Dan" is a man's name (short for Daniel).

ex: We often go biking in the mountains in summer.
Biking to work saves money and time.
She loves biking along the river after work.
Mountain biking can be dangerous without a helmet.
biking.note: Usually means riding a bicycle: "go biking." Uncountable (not "a biking").

ex: Workers used a concrete vibrator to remove air bubbles.
This hand-held vibrator is good for a back massage.
The game controller has a small vibrator inside it.
The vibrator in my phone stopped working after I dropped it.
vibrator.note: In everyday English this word often means a sex toy, so be careful.

ex: He plays the trombone in the school band.
The trombone is a loud brass instrument.
She practices the trombone every evening after school.
I bought a used trombone online for my son.
The movie was a silly melodrama about lost love.
My grandmother loves old black-and-white melodramas.
This TV series is a melodrama with many tears.
The show turned into a melodrama in the last season.
I go to pilates class twice a week.
Doing pilates every day helps my back pain.
She teaches pilates at a gym near my house.
Pilates makes your body stronger and more flexible.
The separatists want to create their own country.
Separatists attacked a police station near the border.
He was arrested as a separatist leader.
The government refused to talk to the separatists.
I cut a kiwi in half and ate it with a spoon.
Kiwis are green inside with tiny black seeds.
She put kiwi slices in the fruit salad.
Can you buy some kiwis at the market for breakfast?
kiwi.note: Also "kiwi fruit." "Kiwi" can also mean a bird or a person from New Zealand.

ex: She has a part-time job at a coffee shop.
I work part-time while I study at college.
Are there any part-time jobs for students here?
My mother works part-time, three days a week.
part-time.note: Opposite: "full-time." Say "a part-time job" or "work part-time."

ex: Turn down the thermostat before you go to bed.
We put a smart thermostat in the living room.
Our office thermostat is always set too low.
Who changed the thermostat in the kitchen again?
He trades derivatives at a big bank in London.
Derivatives can be very risky for small investors.
The bank lost a lot of money on derivatives.
Options and futures are two kinds of derivatives.
derivative.note: Most often it means something made from another thing: "Gasoline is a derivative of oil."

ex: A gazelle can run very fast to escape lions.
The lion chased the young gazelle across the grass.
We saw many gazelles on our safari in Africa.
She is tall and runs like a gazelle.
She grows dahlias in her garden every year.
These dahlia flowers are bright red and very big.
I bought some dahlias at the market this morning.
Dahlias bloom in late summer and early fall.
Free lunch is one benefit of working here.
The job pays well and has good benefits.
Health insurance is the most important benefit for me.
Does this company offer any benefits to part-time workers?
benefit.note: Most often "benefit" means a good result or advantage: "the benefits of exercise."

sparring.note: Uncountable: say "sparring" or "a sparring session," not "a sparring."

ex: We need a bigger dataset for this project.
Download the dataset and open it in a spreadsheet.
The dataset has ten thousand rows of sales data.
She cleaned the dataset before she started the analysis.

mana.note: Uncountable: a lot of mana (not "a mana").

ex: She got a job in pharma after college.
Big pharma makes huge profits from new drugs.
The pharma company is testing a new drug.
Ads for pharma products are common on TV.
She speaks Urdu with her family at home.
Urdu is one of the main languages of Pakistan.
The sign at the station was written in Urdu.
He is taking an Urdu class at the university.
The steward brought us coffee and some cookies.
He works as a steward on a big cruise ship.
Can you ask the steward for an extra blanket?
The steward showed us to our cabin on the ship.
steward.note: Also means a person who manages or looks after something. On planes, "flight attendant" is more common.

ex: He plays forward for our city hockey team.
The forward scored two goals in the first half.
Our best forward is injured and can't play today.
The team needs a fast forward who can score.
forward.note: Most often "forward" means toward the front: "Please move forward."

ex: The country was called the aggressor in the war.
The aggressor attacked the town without any warning.
The world must work together to stop the aggressor.
In the fight at school, he was clearly the aggressor.
